transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hi Mr. Park, thanks for coming back in to see me. I asked to meet because I found a mistake in your discharge paperwork from yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I listed a follow-up appointment for you at the Westside Clinic, but that clinic does not take your insurance provider. I gave you the wrong referral. I am very sorry, and I take full responsibility for this error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I messed up the insurance check before writing the instructions. Does that make sense, or should I clarify how the referral process works?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, it makes sense. But I already spent two hours on the phone with them this morning trying to figure out why my card wasn't working. They told me I couldn't even book the appointment.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that's frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating? I'm nineteen! I don't even know how this stuff works! I thought I was doing everything right and then I get told I can't see the doctor I'm supposed to see. Who is going to pay for this if I just went there?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You won't be charged for a clinic you can't access. I really apologize for the stress this caused. Just to be sure we are on the same page, do you understand that the Westside Clinic is not an option for your care?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I get it! I get that I can't go there! Why did this happen? Were you just not paying attention?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I was not thorough enough in checking your insurance coverage against the clinic's list. That is my fault.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. I'm trying to handle this on my own and now I have to start over. I don't even know where else to go. I feel like I'm just being pushed around by the system.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like you feel overwhelmed and unsupported right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am overwhelmed! I'm terrified that if I don't get this follow-up, whatever is wrong with me is just going to get worse and I'm just sitting here with a piece of paper that is useless!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you're scared about your health getting worse because of this delay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly! So what now? Do I just wait another week? Do I call ten more places?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm going to help you find a new clinic today. I'll start by calling the internal coordination team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's it? You're just going to call someone? I spent my whole morning on the phone and now I'm sitting here in another appointment. I should be in class.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know your time is valuable, but we need to get this right.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't understand how a doctor can just write a name on a paper without checking if it actually works. It's so careless.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're right, it was careless. I apologize again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't even know if I trust you guys to get the next one right.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand why you'd feel that way. I'm going to make sure the next referral is verified by two different staff members.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine. So when am I actually going to have an appointment?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a date this second, but I'll call the coordinator now and I will email you a confirmed address and time by 5:00 PM today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And if you don't?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will. If you don't see an email by 5:00, please call my direct line.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't even have your direct line.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll write it down for you right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is just a mess. I can't believe I have to deal with this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's a lot. Look, I have to go check on another patient now, so let's wrap up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, you're just leaving? I still don't have the name of the new place.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, I'm going to find the place first so I don't make the same mistake twice. I'll get that email to you by five.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is just great.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry for the trouble. I'll get on this immediately.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language at the end of the encounter ('let's wrap up') to terminate the conversation.

E.justification: The error was explicitly named in the first turn, lay language was used, and comprehension was checked twice ('Does that make sense', 'do you understand').

A.justification: The resident used direct apology language and took full personal responsibility ('I take full responsibility', 'That is my fault') without deflection.

R.justification: The resident named specific emotions back to the patient twice ('overwhelmed and unsupported', 'scared about your health getting worse').

T.justification: The resident provided a specific next step with a timeline (email by 5:00 PM), a patient role (call direct line if no email), and a prevention strategy (verified by two staff members).
